**Fig. 1** Study design. Study 1 evaluated ten detectors once on the locked UWHVF test split, on true no-change series (Artes retest data) and in an external clinic (GRAPE). Study 2, specified in a new protocol, used 5-fold patient-level cross-fitting across all UWHVF eyes with at least eight tests, held every detector to the same false-alarm rate by shuffle calibration, added detectors that control false alarms over repeated reviews, and tested local recalibration in GRAPE. UWHVF, University of Washington Humphrey Visual Field data set.

**Fig. 2** Study 1. Sensitivity against the future-confirmed reference ({{n:sens:D1:3}} progressors) versus false-alarm rate on true no-change series, by number of tests. Each point is one detector (D1–D10, defined in Methods); bars are 95% confidence intervals from a patient-level bootstrap. The shaded band marks false-alarm rates at or below the nominal 5% (dashed line). Note the different horizontal scales.

**Fig. 3** Study 2. Sensitivity ({{qn:sens:D1:3}} cross-fitted progressors) versus false-alarm rate on true no-change series, by number of tests. Shuffle-calibrated (SC) detectors were set to 5% false alarms on shuffled series of the clinic's own records; B8 is the same LightGBM model as S5 with the usual threshold (95% specificity on labelled stable eyes). Bars are 95% confidence intervals. At matched false alarms (shaded band), no detector was significantly more sensitive than the trend test D1.

**Fig. 4** Study 2, repeated reviews. Share of progressors flagged at least once by the sixth test versus share of true no-change series flagged at least once over the reviews at three to six tests. D1 and D7 applied at every review are compared with detectors designed to keep cumulative false alarms at 5% (Q1–Q4, defined in Methods). Bars are 95% confidence intervals.
